# NetSuite says the record already exists {#duplicate-records}

Find the existing record before deciding whether to add a new one or update what is already there.

<CsvGuideContext slug="duplicate-records" />

## A custom record already uses this identifier {#a-custom-record-already-uses-this-identifier}

**Message looks like**

- `Custom Record`

The wording identifies a matching situation, not a confirmed diagnosis for your account.

**What it means**

Another record uses this identifier.

Import context: General imports.

**Check this first**

Check existing external IDs.

::: details Show the steps

**Steps for this error**

1. Search the custom-record type for the external ID or name used by the failed row.
2. Decide whether the row should update that record or create a different one.
3. Use Update with the existing record’s verified identifier, or assign a genuinely new identifier for Add.

:::

<CsvEntryHelp entry-id="GEN-11" />

- [General Import Errors](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_4568642498.html)

Documentation checked September 16, 2026.

## An entity already uses this external ID {#an-entity-already-uses-this-external-id}

**Message looks like**

- `entity`

The wording identifies a matching situation, not a confirmed diagnosis for your account.

**What it means**

Another entity may already own that external ID.

Import context: Leads and prospects.

**Check this first**

Search entities by the value and establish which record the import is meant to create or update.

::: details Show the steps

**Check the record reference**

1. Find the field named in the error on the import's Field Mapping page.
2. Open its edit control and check the selected reference type.
3. Compare that setting with the actual CSV value. A number could be a name, an external ID, or an internal ID. Its appearance alone does not establish the type.
4. Locate the intended record in the same account. Confirm its identity and whether it is available for this transaction.
5. Correct the file or mapping so they agree. Use a default only when it applies to every affected row.

If you need to see internal IDs, enable them in your personal preferences or include them in a saved-search export. Supported reference types vary by field. Name matching is generally case-insensitive, so changing capitalization alone should not be the standard recommendation.

[Reference types](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N349594.html)

For a duplicate-record message, determine whether you intend to update the existing record or create a different one. Do not generate new external IDs simply to get past the error. For inactive records or subsidiary restrictions, verify the intended business setup before changing it. Those are account decisions, not text-cleanup operations.

:::

<CsvEntryHelp entry-id="REL-03" />

- [General Relationship Import Errors](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_4570061540.html)

Documentation checked September 16, 2026.

## The transaction already exists {#the-transaction-already-exists}

**Message looks like**

- `record already exists`

The wording identifies a matching situation, not a confirmed diagnosis for your account.

**What it means**

The identifier may belong to an earlier transaction.

Import context: Transactions.

**Check this first**

Find it before creating another.

::: details Show the steps

**Steps for this error**

1. Search the target transaction type for the external ID or transaction identifier in the failed row.
2. Decide whether the row is a new transaction or an update to the one found.
3. Use the verified existing identifier for Update, or supply a new unique identifier for Add.

:::

<CsvEntryHelp entry-id="TXN-03" />

- [General Transaction Import Errors](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_4570011199.html)

Documentation checked September 16, 2026.
